arxiv-2009-00543.title: Nonlocal Kondo effect and quantum critical phase in heavy fermion metals
arxiv-2009-00543.creator: Jiangfan Wang, Yi-feng Yang
arxiv-2009-00543.description: Abstract Heavy fermion metals typically exhibit unconventional quantum critical point or quantum critical phase at zero temperature due to competition of Kondo effect and magnetism. Previous theories were often based on certain local type of assumptions and a fully consistent explanation of experiments has not been achieved.

arxiv-2103-00706.title: From nanotubes to nanoholes: scaling of selectivity in uniformly charged nanopores through the Dukhin number for 1:1 electrolytes
arxiv-2103-00706.creator: Zsófia Sarkadi, Dávid Fertig, Zoltán Ható, Mónika Valiskó, Dezső Boda
arxiv-2103-00706.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zsófia Sarkadi, Dávid Fertig, Zoltán Ható, Mónika Valiskó, Dezső Boda. Scaling of the behavior of a nanodevice means that the device function (selectivity) is a unique smooth and monotonic function of a scaling parameter that is an appropriate combination of the system’s parameters.

arxiv-2106-10197.title: A Dynamic Spatial-temporal Attention Network for Early Anticipation of Traffic Accidents
arxiv-2106-10197.creator: Muhammad Monjurul Karim, Yu Li, Ruwen Qin 1, Member, Zhaozheng Yin, Senior Member
arxiv-2106-10197.description: Abstract The rapid advancement of sensor technologies and artificial intelligence are creating new opportunities for traffic safety enhancement. Dashboard cameras (dashcams) have been widely deployed on both human driving vehicles and automated driving vehicles. A computational intelligence model that can accurately and promptly predict accidents from the dashcam video will enhance the preparedness for accident prevention.

arxiv-2211-13689.title: Open Superstring First Mass Level Effective Lagrangian: Massive Spin-2 in an Electromagnetic Background
arxiv-2211-13689.description: Abstract Minimal coupling leads to problems such as loss of causality if one wants to describe charged particles of spin greater than one propagating in a constant electromagnetic background. Regge trajectories in string theory contain such states, so their study may allow us to investigate possible avenues to remedy the pathologies.

arxiv-2309-10211.title: Loop Polarity Analysis to Avoid Underspecification in Deep Learning
arxiv-2309-10211.creator: Donald Martin, Jr, David Kinney
arxiv-2309-10211.description: Abstract . Deep learning is a powerful set of techniques for detecting complex patterns in data. However, when the causal structure of that process is underspecified, deep learning models can be brittle, lacking robustness to shifts in the distribution of the data-generating process.

arxiv-2410-18874.title: Diffusion of impurities in a moderately dense confined granular gas
arxiv-2410-18874.creator: Rubén Gómez González, Vicente Garzó, Ricardo Brito, Rodrigo Soto
arxiv-2410-18874.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Rubén Gómez González, Vicente Garzó, Ricardo Brito, Rodrigo Soto. Mass transport of impurities immersed in a confined quasi-two-dimensional moderately dense granular gas of inelastic hard spheres is studied. The effect of the confinement on granular particles is modeled through a collisional model (the so-called Δ \Delta -model) that includes an effective mechanism to transfer the kinetic energy injected by vibration in the vertical direction to the horizontal degrees of freedom of grains.

arxiv-2503-18848.title: The isoscalar octet axial form factor of the nucleon from lattice QCD
arxiv-2503-18848.creator: Alessandro Barone, Dalibor Djukanovic, Georg von Hippel, Jonna Koponen, Harvey B. Meyer, Konstantin Ottnad, Hartmut Wittig
arxiv-2503-18848.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alessandro Barone, Dalibor Djukanovic, Georg von Hippel, Jonna Koponen, Harvey B. Meyer, Konstantin Ottnad, Hartmut Wittig. The isoscalar axial-vector form factor of the nucleon plays a key role in understanding the electroweak interaction of nucleons. For the interpretation of the spin structure of the nucleon the non-singlet isoscalar axial charge is indispensable.

arxiv-2602-15306.title: Sparse Additive Model Pruning for Order-Based Causal Structure Learning
arxiv-2602-15306.creator: Kentaro Kanamori, Hirofumi Suzuki, Takuya Takagi
arxiv-2602-15306.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Kentaro Kanamori, Hirofumi Suzuki, Takuya Takagi. Causal structure learning, also known as causal discovery, aims to estimate causal relationships between variables as a form of a causal directed acyclic graph (DAG) from observational data. One of the major frameworks is the order-based approach that first estimates a topological order of the underlying DAG and then prunes spurious edges from the fully-connected DAG induced by the estimated topological order.

pmc-11426820.title: Evaluation of the Biocompatibility of Periodontal Dressings: An In Vitro Study
pmc-11426820.creator: Fatema Akhter
pmc-11426820.description: Background:Periodontal dressings play a crucial role in post-operative management of periodontal surgeries by protecting surgical sites and promoting wound healing. Biocompatibility evaluation is essential to ensure the safety and effectiveness of these materials. This study aims to assess the biocompatibility of periodontal dressings through an in vitro approach.

pmc-11749949.title: Outcomes of trauma patients on chronic antithrombotic therapies in a trauma center in a rural state
pmc-11749949.creator: Benjamin Moore, Hanna Jensen, Karan Patel, Zeel Modi, Rebecca J Reif, Shibani Lal, Stephen M Bowman, Melissa Kost, Kyle J Kalkwarf, Joseph Margolick, Avi Bhavaraju, Howard L Corwin
pmc-11749949.description: ObjectiveThe number of trauma patients presenting with chronic antithrombotic therapy is on the rise. The risk of hemorrhage, the leading cause of death in trauma patients, increases for those on such therapy. This study sought to compare the clinical outcomes of patients on warfarin, direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC), or antiplatelet agents.

pmc-12434389.title: In Situ Evaluation of Macrophage Populations and Inflammasome Components in Cutaneous and Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis
pmc-12434389.creator: Caroline de Heleno Chagas de Carvalho, Gabriela Venicia Araujo Flores, Carmen Maria Sandoval Pacheco, Vania Lucia da Ribeiro da Matta, Carolina de Esteves de Morais, Ricardo Romiti, Walter Belda Júnior, Márcia Dalastra Laurenti
pmc-12434389.description: American tegumentary leishmaniasis (ATL) affects the skin and mucous membranes, with a spectrum shaped by Th1/Th2 responses. This study investigated inflammasome activation in correlation with macrophage subpopulations, tissue parasitism, and histological changes in cutaneous and mucocutaneous leishmaniasis. We assessed inflammasome activation, tissue parasitism, and macrophage populations by immunohistochemistry, correlating with histopathological alterations using 29 biopsies from cutaneous and mucocutaneous leishmaniasis.

pmc-12610231.title: Modeling the Influence of Macronutrients on the Heat Resistance of Salmonella in Milk Powder
pmc-12610231.creator: Xinyao Wei, Yi Lian, Shuxiang Liu, Ki Sun Yoon
pmc-12610231.description: Multiple Salmonella outbreaks linked to milk powders call for the need for effective pasteurization processes. Understanding the thermal inactivation kinetics of Salmonella in milk powder is crucial; however, the influence of macronutrient content (protein, fat, and carbohydrate) on these kinetics remains unclear.

pmc-12611063.title: Bone Formation and Anti-Inflammatory Properties of Iodine-Loaded Titanium Implants: An Animal Study
pmc-12611063.creator: Kazuto Yamada, Kazuya Inoue, Nanako Shimada, Tatsuya Kakutani, Yasuhisa Sawai, Naoko Imagawa-Fujimura, Kayoko Yamamoto, Nahoko Kato-Kogoe, Seiji Yamaguchi, Takaaki Ueno, Wojciech Simka
pmc-12611063.description: Titanium implants are subjected to various surface treatments to improve their in vivo function. In this study, we evaluated the usefulness of titanium implants treated with acid, NaOH, CaCl2, heat, and ICl3 (Ac-NaCaThIo) in terms of in vivo bone-bonding strength, bone formation, and histological anti-inflammatory properties.

pmc-12983803.title: Letter regarding ‘early intervention with rescue ERCP and pancreatic stenting for unanticipated post-ERCP pancreatitis: a comparative study’
pmc-12983803.creator: ibrahim Ethem Güven
pmc-12983803.description: ell-known and frequently used method in cases of difficult cannulation, unintended cannulation of the pancreatic duct, and in high-risk patients [2]. However, treatment options in unanticipated PEP are still controversial [3]. In this context, the authors present significant data indicating that early rescue ERCP with pancreatic duct stenting may improve clinical outcomes in selected patients with unanticipated PEP.

pmc-13210429.title: Comparative Study of Plasticized Polyvinyl Alcohol and Hydroxypropyl Methylcellulose Films for Pharmaceutical Applications: Mechanical, Thermal, Structural and Disintegration Properties
pmc-13210429.creator: Rittin Abraham Kurien, Gokul Kannan, Wantanwa Krongrawa, Supakij Suttiruengwong, Pornsak Sriamornsak
pmc-13210429.description: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) films plasticized with glycerin or polyethylene glycol (PEG) were investigated to elucidate structure–property relationships in hydrophilic polymeric film systems. Films were prepared by solution casting at a fixed polymer concentration of 2.7% w/w with plasticizer contents ranging from 0.49 to 1.33% w/w, yielding continuous, free-standing films with good surface integrity.

pmc-13236757.title: Application of LC-MS/MS methods and risk assessment for selected emerging contaminants and their transformation products in a sub-Adriatic river system
pmc-13236757.creator: Aleksander Kravos, Helena Prosen
pmc-13236757.description: The present study investigates solid-phase extraction (SPE) followed by LC-MS/MS for the analysis of contaminants of emerging concern (CECs) and transformation products (TPs) in the Slovenian-Italian Vipava river system (part of the Adriatic Sea catchment). The adapted method enabled quantitative analysis of 13 various CECs and qualitative analysis of 2 UV filters.

pmc-13478454.title: Deep learning embedded latent class joint modelling of time-to-event and longitudinal data
pmc-13478454.creator: Tristan John Elers Harris, Najmeh Nakhaei Rad, Sphiwe Bonakele Skhosana
pmc-13478454.description: Joint modelling of longitudinal and time-to-event data is a powerful tool for analysing complex medical data. Joint latent class models (JLCMs), in particular, provide additional prognostic insight by clustering subjects into latent subgroups within a mixture of experts framework. Traditionally, the mixing proportions are modelled using a multinomial logistic regression.

pmc-13532961.title: Circular RNAs: Unlocking new avenues in cardiometabolic disease management
pmc-13532961.creator: Kimberley M. Mellor, Thomas D. Donelly, Gerald L.M. Naepi, Glenn D. Wadley, Bianca C. Bernardo
pmc-13532961.description: Cardiometabolic diseases refer to a group of interrelated conditions that affect both the cardiovascular system and metabolic processes. These conditions represent a significant global health burden and often share common risk factors such as obesity, high cholesterol and insulin resistance. Cardiometabolic diseases include conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, coronary artery disease and stroke.

pmc-13600389.title: Infants Younger Than 24 Months With Severe Malaria Have a Serologic Profile of Active Infection With Epstein-Barr Virus
pmc-13600389.creator: Wayne T Cheng, Balotin Fogang, Aarti Jain, D Huw Davies, Philip L Felgner, Carole Eboumbou, Paul N Koki, Samuel H Speck, Chester J Joyner, Lawrence S Ayong, Tracey J Lamb
pmc-13600389.description: BackgroundPrimary Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection occurs during late adolescence and is characterized by the symptomatic manifestation of infectious mononucleosis. Asymptomatic primary EBV infection in malaria-endemic areas often occurs in young children by the age of 2 years. Resulting in humoral immune suppression to unrelated antigenic challenges for approximately 4 weeks.

pmc-13633996.title: Corneal topographic changes after upper eyelid blepharoplasty prior to cataract surgery
pmc-13633996.creator: Kleopatra Varna-Tigka, Sophia Göhring, Myriam Böhm, Yaroslava Wenner, Thomas Kohnen
pmc-13633996.description: PurposeTo investigate the effect of upper eyelid blepharoplasty (UEB) on corneal topography in cataract patients using Scheimpflug technology.MethodsThis prospective single-center, longitudinal study included 88 eyes of 45 patients undergoing UEB for dermatochalasis prior to cataract surgery. Scheimpflug imaging (Pentacam®AXL, Wetzlar), was performed preoperatively and at two weeks and three months postoperatively.
